newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban commander sees no peaceful solution.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban commander sees no peaceful solution.

text.p: A senior military commander of Afghanistan's Taleban movement said on Wednesday the purist Islamic group would not negotiate with opposition forces to end the long conflict.
"We will not consider negotiations with our enemies... and declare that war is the sole way to end it," Taleban's commander for central Afghanistan Abdul Wahid told reporters.

The Taleban, which captured the capital Kabul last September and controls more than two-thirds of the war-shattered country, faces an alliance of forces commanded by ousted government commander Ahmad Shah Masood, northern Uzbek chief General Abdul Rashid Dostum and the Shi'ite group Hezb-i-Wahdat.

The largely ethnic Pushtun and Sunni Moslem Taleban has been stalled for nearly three months in the foothills of Hindu Kush mountains on the vital Salang-Kabul highway 95 km (60 miles) north of Kabul, where Dostum has blown up a bridge to block any advance to his northern provinces.
Masood has dynamited a gorge of his native Pansher Valley, east of Salang, and Wahdat has so far blocked passage to the north through the strategic Shibar Pass in central Afghanistan.
The Taleban has vowed to take the rest of Afghanistan in pursuing what it calls a "heavenly" duty to rid the country of corruption.
Wahid said his forces had not lost any territory or men in any fighting in recent days.
Talking to reporters in Ghorband Valley, 160 km (100 miles) north of Kabul, Wahid said an implementation of Sharia Islamic law in the whole of the country was Taleban's agenda.
So far Taleban has shown little interest in talks with their opponents after successive victories against the forces of ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani and his allies.
But it has not formally ruled out a peaceful settlement through mediation or negotiation.
